newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn seen steady to one cent lower, spillover.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn seen steady to one cent lower, spillover.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were expected to open steady to one cent per bushel lower, under modest pressure from spillover losses in other markets, traders said.
However, total net weekly exports sales of 1.0 million tonnes of corn were expected to offer support. Both new and old crop sales were in line with trade expectations.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture also announced a sale of 150,000 tonnes of U.S. corn to unknown on Thursday, which could also support prices, traders said.
Traders said data from the International Grains Council was slightly bearish for corn.
The IGC put total coarse grain output at a record 903 million tonnes. The increase was prompted primarily by expectations for an increase in U.S. corn production, the agency said.
